svg.title: Antibiotic targets and resistance
svg.desc: Where the main classes of antibiotic act on a Gram-negative bacterial cell: the outer membrane (polymyxins), the cell wall (beta-lactams; glycopeptides in Gram-positives), the cell membrane (daptomycin, in Gram-positives), DNA replication (quinolones), protein synthesis on the ribosome (aminoglycosides, macrolides, tetracyclines) and folate synthesis (trimethoprim, sulfonamides); and five ways bacteria resist: enzymes that break the drug down, efflux pumps, an altered target, fewer porins, and resistance genes passed on plasmids.
